title: analytics — codebase report
summary: Plausible Analytics is a web analytics service. Its server is an Elixir and Phoenix app. A small JavaScript tracker script sends page views to it, and a React dashboard reads the reports. The repo holds 2,129 files and 709,883 lines, with 4,446 commits since 2019-09-02. Postgres stores accounts and sites, and ClickHouse stores events and sessions. A newcomer should start with lib/plausible_web/router.ex, then follow one pageview through the ingestion code and one report through the stats code. All 15 charts are present. The module import chart covers only JavaScript and TypeScript, because the measurement skips Elixir imports.

diagrams.title: The stack
diagrams.text: The browser sends events to the Phoenix web layer. The Elixir core turns them into sessions and writes batches to ClickHouse. Account data lives in Postgres, and the Oban workers (a background job library) call Google Analytics 4, send email and write imported rows. Start here to see which part talks to which.

diagrams.title: Lines of code by directory
diagrams.text: The repo holds 709,883 lines in 2,129 files. The fixture directory alone has 308,671 lines (43%), mostly JSON used by tests. Next come test/plausible_web with 83,604 lines and priv/ua_inspector with 67,720 lines. The 2,129 files are rolled up to 40 boxes, and the smaller directories are in "(other)", 11,956 lines. Real application code is mainly lib/plausible_web (33,971 lines) and lib/plausible (32,896 lines).

diagrams.title: Languages by lines
diagrams.text: JSON is the largest language by lines, with 323,370 lines. Elixir follows with 235,913 lines in 1,315 files. YAML has 73,215 lines and TypeScript has 47,982. The seven smallest languages (JavaScript, SQL, Markdown, CSS, Shell, TOML, PHP) are shown as "Other", 12,076 lines. The fixture directory holds 308,671 of those JSON lines, so Elixir is the main language of the application code.

diagrams.title: Largest commits and newest releases
diagrams.text: The repo has 4,446 commits and 671 tags. The chart shows the five commits that changed the most lines and the 15 newest tags, from v3.0.0-rc.0 on 2025-04-08 to v3.2.1 on 2026-05-15. The largest commit removed the Universal Analytics import logic and changed 865,919 lines on 2024-07-05. The Erlang and Elixir upgrade on 2023-10-24 changed 843,728 lines.

diagrams.title: Recording a pageview
diagrams.text: The tracker script posts to /api/event, which ExternalController handles. The ingestion code builds a request, asks GateKeeper if the site may send events, and runs the event through a list of steps. Any step can drop the event. A kept event goes to the session cache, then to the event write buffer, which flushes to ClickHouse. The controller answers 202 once the event is buffered.

diagrams.title: Loading a dashboard report
diagrams.text: The dashboard posts a query to /api/stats/:domain/query. A plug checks that the user may see the site. StatsController parses the parameters and builds a Query, which runs through a chain of checks. QueryRunner then optimizes the query, builds SQL and reads the rows from ClickHouse. The controller sends the result back as JSON.

diagrams.title: How an event joins a session
diagrams.text: The session cache looks up a session by user id, then by the previous salt user id. An engagement event only refreshes a session that exists, and is dropped if there is none. Any other event updates the found session or starts a new one. An update writes the old row with sign -1 and the new row with sign 1, so ClickHouse can collapse the rows. A cached session is reused only if it is at most 30 minutes old.

diagrams.title: Data model across Postgres and ClickHouse
diagrams.text: Postgres holds the account side: teams, users, memberships, subscriptions, sites, goals and site imports. A team owns many sites and has one subscription. ClickHouse holds events_v2 and sessions_v2, which link to a site by site_id. The chart lists only the columns that carry the relations and a few key fields.

diagrams.title: Plausible routes
diagrams.text: The router has public pages, signed-in pages and HTTP APIs. Public pages are register, login and shared dashboards. Signed-in pages cover the site list, new site, installation, the site dashboard, settings and billing. The APIs include the events API, the internal stats API, the public stats API v1 and v2, and the plugins API. The sites API under /api/v1/sites is compiled only in the enterprise build.

diagrams.title: Site import lifecycle
diagrams.text: A site import has four statuses: pending, importing, completed and failed. A new import starts as pending. The worker moves it to importing when the job starts. It ends as completed if all rows are imported, or failed if the import returns an error.

diagrams.title: Adding a first site
diagrams.text: The chart follows a site owner from sign-up to the first dashboard view. The email activation step and the tracker script step are the weakest, with scores of 3 and 2. The site status moves from new_site through verification_succeeded and first_pageview to completed. Installation support, a headless browser check in the tracker folder, verifies the script.

diagrams.title: Importing Google Analytics 4 data
diagrams.text: The user picks a property and dates. The controller clamps the dates, creates a pending import and rejects the request if another import runs. The Oban worker fetches the GA4 reports and writes rows to ClickHouse through a buffer. On success it marks the import completed. On error it purges the imported rows and marks it failed. Either way it sends an email to the user.

diagrams.title: Hot files: size against edits
diagrams.text: Each bubble is one of the 40 most edited files out of 1,249 files edited between 2025-10-29 and 2026-10-29. The x axis is lines, the y axis is commits, and the bubble size is bytes. CHANGELOG.md has the most edits, 63. The router has 54 edits and 770 lines. The large test files are big but change less.

diagrams.title: Module imports (JavaScript and TypeScript only)
diagrams.text: The 1,082 file imports are rolled up to 191 links between 40 directories, up to 5 levels deep. The measurement covers JavaScript and TypeScript only, so the Elixir code is not in this chart. Most links lie in assets/js/dashboard, and its subfolders import the dashboard root often. The strongest link is tracker/test to tracker/test/support, with 65 imports. The next is stats/graph to the dashboard root, with 33.

diagrams.title: Files that change together
diagrams.text: The chart shows the 30 most frequent of 55,475 file pairs that changed in the same commit. Commits that touch more than 50 files are skipped, which removed 23 commits. The top pair is site_controller.ex and its test, with 84 commits. CHANGELOG.md pairs with several controllers, and several controllers pair with their own test files.
